bug_fixed_2026-09-07.description: Found via carrier/lift/harness/GCC_X87.md SS4: line_intersect's ua/ub NaN guards (D==0 && numerator==0, i.e. segments sharing their start point) were written as `if (!(ua >= 0.0)) return 0;` / `if (!(ub >= 0.0)) return 0;`, which reject on NaN because `NaN >= 0.0` is false and the negation is true. The original x87 code's fucom/fnstsw/test $0x45,%ah/je idiom only branches on the ORDERED true case, so a NaN ua/ub falls through every guard uncaught; the original then runs a masked fistp on NaN+0.5 (integer indefinite 0x80000000), writes garbage coordinates, and returns EAX=1, whereas the un-fixed source returned EAX=0 on those vectors -- a toolchain-independent mismatch (948-1011 of every 20000 vectors, identical across every MSVC and GCC build tried, unrelated to floating-point precision). Fix: rewrote the two guards as `if (ua < 0.0) return 0;` / `if (ub < 0.0) return 0;` (matching the already-correct `ua > 1.0` / `ub > 1.0` guards) so C's IEEE-754 comparison semantics reproduce the same NaN-falls-through behaviour as the hardware's unordered fucom, with no change to arithmetic order or to the pre-existing x87 double-vs-80-bit precision gap.

gcc.note: The double-vs-80-bit gravity-sum gap MSVC shows (above) is fully closed under GCC -mfpmath=387 -mno-sse2 -O2 (0 of 80000 differ at Tplayer+0x18/sy's gravity chain). The 7/80000 residual is a DIFFERENT, much narrower wrinkle: in every one of the 7 vectors, sx or sy was fed a genuine SIGNALING NaN (IEEE-754 exponent all-1s, mantissa top bit i.e. bit 51 clear, at least one other mantissa bit set) via the vector generator's random-bit-pattern pool; the clamp chain correctly leaves the value untouched either way (neither '<' nor '>' is true for NaN, matching C semantics), but the ORIGINAL binary's exact instruction encoding preserves the signaling bit while GCC -O2's own instruction selection for the same source-level comparison chain quiets it (sets bit 51) as an incidental side effect of whichever x87 compare/move sequence it chooses -- confirmed byte-for-byte: every differing byte is exactly +8 (a single bit, bit 51) at Tplayer+0x16 (sx byte 6) or +0x1e (sy byte 6), never anywhere else, and every other field (x, y, status, bounce, and the payload's other 63 bits) matches exactly. A legitimate game double can never BECOME a signaling NaN through ordinary IEEE-754 arithmetic (only quiet NaNs ever propagate that way), so this has no reachable gameplay consequence; reported per win32_pilot.md's 'never a percentage, always the exact byte' rule rather than chased into GCC's instruction-selection internals, which plain C source cannot control without inline asm (purity-gate-banned).
